title: 第七章　基础设施作用于时间

zh: 第七章　基础设施作用于时间
en: 7 Infrastructures Work on Time

zh: 基础设施承诺增强我们对空间的控制。公路、航运运河、铁路、电网和数据网络体现了各种地球改造式的变动；如我们在
所述，人类主要在过去一个半世纪里通过这些变动改造了地球。
反过来，通过征服空间，基础设施增强了对时间的掌控，加快了能源、数据、货物和人员流动的速度。这种加速也许是我们表达资本主义现代性体验的最常见方式。
en: Infrastructures promise to increase our control over space. Highways, ship canals, railways, power grids, and data networks embody the kinds of terraforming modifications through which, largely over the last century and a half, as we noted in
, humans have transformed the Earth.

By conquering space, in turn, infrastructures increase the command of time, speeding up the rate at which energy, data, goods, and people flow. This acceleration is perhaps the most common way in which we express the experience of capitalist modernity.

zh: 然而，基础设施在与资本化的关系中扮演着不同角色。这些塑造地球的大型项目与时间还有另一种关系；没有这种关系，我们今天所知的资本化将会崩溃。基础设施的产生不是为了加速，而是为了引入一种延迟。从这个角度看，基础设施的优点不是加速时间，而是能够把未来推得更远。这一思路改变了我们对资本的理解，也改变了我们对现代人类为何要改造自身与地球之关系的理解。它还使我们能够重新思考气候变化、栖息地破坏和物种灭绝危机的政治。要考察这一点，我们必须从颠倒我们思考基础设施如何作用于时间的方式开始。
en: However, infrastructures have a different role in relation to capitalisation. These large, Earth-shaping projects have another relationship to time, without which capitalisation, as we know it today, would collapse. Infrastructures are brought into being not to speed things up but to introduce a delay. The virtue of infrastructure is not the acceleration of time, from this perspective, but the ability to place the future further away. This approach changes our understanding of capital and the purposes for which modern humans modify their relations with the Earth. It also enables us to rethink the politics of climate change, the destruction of habitat, and the crisis of species extinction. To consider this, we need to start from a reversal of the way we think about how infrastructures work on time.

zh: 关于基础设施的常规写法从空间问题出发，把时间视为结果。基础设施创造通道和连接，把分散的点联系起来，便利其间的移动。中国政府 2013 年发起的“一带一路”倡议，为连接亚洲、非洲和欧洲各地的公路、铁路
、海港和电站建设提供融资，例证了基础设施与征服距离之间的这种联系。作为世界各地正在建设的若干“超大走廊”中最大的一个，其推动者强调大陆之间的相互连接和海洋之间的相互连通。
然而，这种把基础设施视为征服空间方式的关注，掩盖了建设基础设施时往往最重要的东西。
en: The standard way of writing about infrastructure is to start from the question of space and treat time as a consequence. Infrastructures create channels and connections that link separate points, facilitating movement between them. China’s Belt and Road Initiative, launched by the Chinese government in 2013 to finance the building of roads, rail lines,

seaports, and power stations connecting locations across Asia, Africa, and Europe, exemplifies this association between infrastructure and the command of distance. As the largest of several ‘mega-corridors’ under construction around the world, its promoters emphasised the interlinking of continents and the interconnection of oceans.
Yet this focus on infrastructures as a mode of conquering space obscures what is often most important in building them.

zh: 从常识角度看，对时间控制的增强是征服空间的结果。公路和铁路、管道和集装箱港口、输电线路和通信网络，似乎都提供更快连接的好处。作为我们借以理解资本主义历史的“技术进步”的象征，它们承诺提高流动速率。粮食供应、工人、电力、原油、新闻报道、数据存储、监控和武装力量，都依赖专门建造的网络来克服距离。网络的每一次技术改进和空间延伸，都可能缩短输送一定数量线路所载物资所需的时间。
en: From a common-sense perspective, increased control over time comes as a consequence of the conquest of space. Roads and railways, pipelines and container ports, transmission lines and communication networks all appear to offer the benefit of faster connections. Emblematic of the ‘technical improvement’ through which we understand the history of capitalism, they promise to improve the rate of flow. Food supplies, workers, electrical power, crude petroleum, news reports, data storing, surveillance, and armed force all depend on purpose-built networks to overcome distance. Each technical improvement and spatial extension of the network can reduce the time it takes to convey a given quantity of the material the line carries.

zh: 更快连接和更高流动速率的主张，支持了建设大型基础设施的大多数经济论据。世界银行一项关于“一带一路”倡议的研究，估算新基础设施将产生的效益时，只考虑产品从一国运往另一国速度的提高。
该报告呼应了经济学家中间一个古老但重新流行的论点。对基础设施的大规模投资缩短了货物运输时间，产生的改进被衡量为人类福利的增加，并促成了“明天会更好”的承诺。
en: The claim of faster connections and improved rates of flow supports most economic arguments for the building of large infrastructures. A World Bank study of the Belt and Road Initiative estimated the benefits that the new infrastructure would produce by considering only the increasing speed at which products would move from one country to another.

The report echoed an old but newly popular argument among economists. Large investments in infrastructure reduce the time it takes to move goods, producing an improvement that is measured as an increase in human welfare, and contributing to the promise of a better tomorrow.

zh: 从这个角度看，可以证明殖民主义改善了被殖民者的生活。例如，英国企业家在殖民地印度修建的铁路缩短了运输农产品的时间和成本——使地主得以提高主要市场作物的价格并增加地租。在最近一项关于这一过程的研究中，价格上涨被假定为福利增加的衡量指标。
这项研究以及另一篇证明十九世纪美国铁路建设带来益处的论文，为作者赢得了美国经济学会的约翰·贝茨·克拉克奖——授予被认为四十岁以下最优秀的经济学家。这类研究有助于基础设施发展所依赖的经济化工作，其
引人注目之处，既在于衡量铁路对价格影响的高超技巧，也在于对其他被广泛研究、却难以通过价格衡量的建设后果的漠视，包括饥荒、流行病、贫困化、生态破坏和种族灭绝。
时间的经济化被呈现为此类大型基础设施项目所带来益处的关键要素。时间与空间相连，因此对前者的经济化或压缩自然与后者相关。
en: From this perspective, colonialism can be shown to have improved the life of the colonised. The railways that British entrepreneurs built across colonial India, for example, reduced the time and thus the cost of shipping agricultural products – allowing landowners to raise the price of the main market crops and increase land rents. In a recent study of this process, the rising prices were assumed to measure an increase in welfare.

This research, and a companion paper demonstrating the benefits that the building of railroads brought to the United States in the nineteenth century, won their author the John Bates Clark Medal of the American Economic Association, awarded to the person considered to be the best economist under forty. Contributing to the work of economisation on which the development of infrastructure depends, such

research is as remarkable for the skill with which it measures the impact of railways on prices, as it is for its obliviousness towards other widely studied effects of their construction not easily measurable via prices, including famine, epidemic disease, impoverishment, ecological destruction, and genocide.

The economisation of time is presented as the key element in the benefits brought by such large infrastructure projects. Time and space are linked, so the economisation or compression of the first is naturally associated with the second.

zh: 对更快连接的关注，使大型基础设施的其他后果可以被当作副作用。正是这种关注，使经济学家的模型能够以价格衡量福利，并在殖民地铁路案例中忽视不平等和饥荒问题，忽视霍乱弧菌和其他病原体的传播，或例如其建设造成的大规模森林砍伐。
为减少脱轨和延误，木制铁路枕木（横枕）平均每七年就必须更换。到 1860 年，全球每年估计生产 1.77 亿根枕木，需要砍伐 88.5 万英亩森林。到 1880 年，每年砍伐面积增至三倍，到 1900 年又增至三倍。森林还因薪柴和沿铁路新路线扩大耕作而被毁。在印度，1860 年代和 1870 年代每年砍伐 7 万英亩森林，到 1890 年代翻倍，导致洪水和侵蚀加剧。
正如我们在
所见埃及灌溉工程的影响一样，这些后果并非只是副作用。基础设施开辟的新空间和走廊，为多种行动者——人类和非人类——提供了更好的连接。它们为人的军队和其他生物的军队创造路线。苏伊士运河的开挖使数百种入侵性海洋生物开始殖民地中海；正如我们所见，运河和水坝让水葫芦堵塞下埃及的水道，印度各河流域也是如此，而携带血吸虫病和钩虫病的螺类与线虫则肆虐乡村。
更便利的连接和更快的旅行时间，适用于所有利用新路线者，而不只是那些移动被运费率、市场价格和基础设施建设产生的其他数字所追踪的人。
en: The focus on faster connections allows other consequences of large infrastructures to be treated as side effects. It is this focus that enables the economists’ models to measure welfare in terms of prices, and in the case of colonial railways to ignore questions of inequality and famine, or the spread of the cholera vibrio and other pathogens, or, for example, the extensive deforestation that their construction caused.

To reduce derailments and delays, wooden railway sleepers (crossties) had to be replaced on average every seven years. By 1860, an estimated 177 million ties were produced each year globally, which required the clearing of 885,000 acres of forest. The area cleared each year had tripled by 1880 and tripled again by 1900. Forests were also destroyed for fuel wood and to expand farming along the new routes served by rail. In India, 70,000 acres of forests were removed each year in the 1860s and 1870s, and double that rate by 1890s, leading to increased flooding and erosion.
As with the impact of irrigation works in Egypt, as we saw in

, such consequences were not just side effects. The new spaces and corridors that infrastructures open allow improved connections for multiple agents, human and nonhuman. They create routes for armies of men and armies of other creatures. The digging of the Suez Canal enabled hundreds of invasive species of marine life to begin to colonise the Mediterranean, just as canals and dams, as we saw, allowed water hyacinth to clog the waterways of Lower Egypt, as it did in the river basins of India, and the snails and nematodes carrying bilharzia and hookworm disease to infest the countryside.

Easier connections and faster travel times apply to all those who take advantage of a new route, not just to those whose movements are tracked by freight rates, market prices, and other numbers generated by the building of infrastructures.

zh: 撇开经济学家关于流动速率改善之益处的傲慢论述所遗漏的东西不谈，还有另一种方式理解基础设施如何作用于时间。基础设施可以产生一种延迟；这种延迟不仅以我们通常想象的方式发生，也构成资本化工作的一部分。
en: Leaving aside what is missing from economists’ hubristic accounts of the benefits of improved rates of flow, there is a different way to understand how infrastructures work on time. Infrastructures can produce a delay; and they do this not only in the way we commonly imagine, but as part of the work of capitalisation.

zh: 任何连接上的改善都带来延迟增加的可能。这可能是一种非计划性后果，其例子广为人知。开通或改善一条路线会创造自身需求。原本可能使用其他方式的交通转向新路线，而原先仅在本地范围内进行的流动，则开始利用更广泛的连接。使用改善路线的车辆可能变得更大、更难操控。由于所有这些原因，新基础设施本应减少的延迟可能反而加剧。
有时，改善所造成的延迟非常戏剧性，这种现象或可称为“长赐号效应”。2015 年，埃及政府完成了苏伊士运河的部分拓宽工程，为其中一段增设平行航道，并拓宽、加深其他河段。船舶最大载重量从 21 万载重吨增至 24 万载重吨（1869 年运河开通时，最大载重量为 5,000 吨）。
该十年初最多运载 1 万个集装箱的集装箱船，如今建造得可运载 2 万多个。更大的船更难操控，尤其是在狭窄航道中，船体排开的水可能把船尾吸向河岸。2021 年 3 月，这种“岸壁效应”可能促成了巨型集装箱船“长赐号”搁浅，堵塞运河六天，使价值数十亿美元的全球商品运输受阻。
en: Any improvement in connections brings the possibility of increased delay. This can be an unplanned consequence, examples of which are well known. Opening or improving a route creates its own demand. Traffic that might have moved using other modes switches to the new route, while movements that enjoyed a local circulation take advantage of wider connections. The vehicles using the improved route may become larger and less manoeuvrable. For all these reasons, the delays that the new infrastructure had promised to reduce can be exacer-bated.

On occasion, the delay created by improvement is dramatic, a phenomenon that might be termed the Ever Given effect. In 2015, the Egyptian government completed a partial enlarging of the Suez Canal, doubling one section of the waterway and widening and deepening other stretches. The maximum tonnage a vessel could carry grew from 210,000 to 240,000 deadweight tons (when the Canal opened in 1869, the maximum was 5,000 tons).

Container ships, which at the start of that decade carried up to 10,000 containers, were now built to carry more than 20,000. Larger ships are less manoeuvrable, especially in narrow channels, where the water displaced by the hull can suck the stern of the vessel towards the bank. In March 2021, this ‘bank effect’ may have contributed to the grounding of the giant container ship Ever Given, which blocked the canal for six days and stranded the global shipment of commodities worth billions of dollars.
body.review: 校注：底本把2015年扩建与最大载重由21万吨提高至24万吨相接叙述。苏伊士运河管理局历史表列2001年为21万吨，2010年已为24万吨，2015年仍为24万吨。因此该吨位提升不宜全归于2015年工程；正文数字和叙述保留。 https://www.suezcanal.gov.eg/English/About/SuezCanal/Pages/CanalCharacteristics.aspx

zh: 超大型基础设施计划通常还关联另一种非计划性后果：建设完工的延迟。在建设最大型项目——水坝、桥梁、运河、隧道、铁路、深海油田——时，工期大幅超期是常态，通常被归咎于技术复杂性、范围变更、异常地质构造或极端气候条件。负责者通常把这些因素说成意外，但它们如此频繁发生，反映的不是知识或经验的缺乏，而是推动者和规划者的自利乐观。
推动基础设施建设的人还必须构建一幅足够简单的世界图景，使基础设施能按计划获得批准。未知和意外不是有待克服的边疆，而是作为资本化要求而生产出来的另一种无知。
en: Very large infrastructure schemes are commonly associated with another form of unplanned consequence: the delay in completing their construction. In building the largest projects – dams, bridges, canals, tunnels, rail lines, deep-offshore oil fields – long overruns are the norm, typically blamed on technical complexity, changes in scope, unusual geological formations, or extreme climate conditions. Those responsible usually describe these elements as unexpected, but they occur so routinely that they reflect not an absence of knowledge or experience but the self-interested optimism of the promoters and planners.

Those who promote the building of infrastructures must also build a picture of a world that is simple enough for the infrastructure to be approved as planned. The unknown and the unexpected are not a frontier to be overcome, but another ignorance produced as a requirement of capitalisation.

zh: 目的与价格
en: Purpose and Price

zh: 然而，与这些非预期结果相反，另一种延迟往往是基础设施项目的真正目的。虽然建设基础设施可以以运送人员或物资的需要为理由，但其主要用途往往是为另一种流动提供载体：资金的流动。十九世纪美国伟大的横贯大陆铁路的推动者宣传这些线路对运输粮食、牛群和人员的重要性，但其价值往往在于作为建设金融网络的手段。用理查德·赖特的话说，铁路的一个主要目的是运送纸张。
en: In contrast to such unintended outcomes, however, a different kind of delay is often the very purpose of an infrastructure project. While the building of infrastructure may be justified by a need to move people or supplies, their principal use is often to provide vehicles for another form of movement: the flow of finance. The promoters of the great transcontinental railways of nineteenth-century America advertised the importance of the lines for shipping grain, cattle, and people, but their value was often as a means to construct financial networks. A main purpose of the railways, as Richard Wright puts it, was to move paper.
body.review: 校注：底本此处及原注015作Richard Wright；《Railroaded》作者实为Richard White，与本章原注006一致。英文底本照录。 https://web.stanford.edu/group/spatialhistory/railroaded/about-author.html

zh: 如我们在
所述，大型基础设施项目以公司债券、银行贷款和股票凭证的形式运送投资票据。它们建成不是为了在空间上运输这些金融工具，而是为了提供创造它们并让它们穿越时间的手段。在这种情形中，制造延迟不是建设基础设施的非预期结果，而是其目标。
en: Large infrastructure projects move investment paper, as we noted in

, in the form of corporate bonds, bank loans, and share certificates. They are built not to transport these financial instruments across space, but to provide the means to create them and carry them through time. In this case, creating the delay is not an unintended outcome of the building of infrastructure, but its goal.

zh: 我们再次可以区分这种情况发生的两种方式。第一，建设基础设施可以成为实施工业破坏的手段：先垄断一条路线，然后拖延其开发或减缓物资流动。例如，二十世纪大部分时间里，中东石油基础设施就是按这一原则建设和运营的。取得该地区石油储量的垄断权的大型石油公司力图最大化的不是石油流量，而是利润流量。更高的利润来自确保石油永远不会太容易获得。为了维持限制供应所能产生的异常高额金融收益，石油公司拖延钻井或完井，阻挠管道建设或扩建，并挑起争端，以便关闭泵站和炼油厂。
托斯丹·凡勃伦在二十世纪初论证，这些以及其他蓄意破坏方法——利用大公司扰乱或干扰产业间复杂相互依赖关系的能力——已经成为现代“工业体系”下赚取商业利润的主要手段。
“蓄意破坏”（sabotage）一词最初大约在同一时期被用来描述工人的力量，特别是操作一国铁路的工人，能够制造轻微技术干扰，从而引发整条铁路线或网络减速或瘫痪。工人能够运用这种伴随现代基础设施和能源系统而来的新力量，
争取更好的工作条件和更高的工资。然而，蓄意破坏最有利可图的运用掌握在大型商号手中，在许多产业中，威胁或实施破坏成为常规的致富手段。
作为资本的托词运作的“技术改进”修辞，使我们无法理解蓄意破坏。
en: Once again, we can distinguish two ways in which this happens. First, the building of infrastructure can be the means to carry out industrial sabotage, by first monopolising a route and then delaying its development or slowing the movement of supplies. For much of the twentieth century, for example, the oil infrastructure of the Middle East was built and run according to this principle. The major oil firms that acquired monopoly rights to the region’s petroleum reserves sought to maximise not the flow of oil but the flow of profits. Higher profits came from ensuring that oil was never too readily available. In order to maintain the extraordinary levels of financial gain that could be generated by restricting the supply, oil firms delayed the drilling or completion of wells, blocked the construction or expansion of pipelines, and triggered disputes that allowed the shutting down of pumping stations and refineries.

Thorstein Veblen argued early in the twentieth century that these and other methods of sabotage, taking advantage of the ability of large firms to disrupt or disturb the complex interdependencies among industries, had become a principal means of making business profit under the modern ‘industrial system’.

The term sabotage had first been used, around the same time, to describe the power of workers, in particular those who ran a country’s railways, to introduce a minor technical disruption that might trigger the slowing or breakdown of an entire rail line or network. Workers were able to use this new power that

came with modern infrastructures and energy systems to campaign for better conditions of work and increased wages. The most profitable use of sabotage, however, was in the hands of large business firms, whose threat or use of sabotage became in many industries a routine method of enrichment.
The trope of ‘technical improvement’ that operates as an alibi of capital distracts us from understanding sabotage.

zh: 第二，除了破坏和干扰行为所能带来的利润之外，基础设施所产生的金融商品与基础设施运载的其他物资有着不同的时间关系。投资价值的来源不是使事物更接近的速度，而是把事物推向未来的延迟。这一特质源于基础设施不仅作为运输装置、还作为支付机制运作。它是一种攫取未来付款的装置，付款形式包括运费、客运票价、港口费、桥梁和公路通行费、水费、燃料费、电费、房产租金、互联网订阅费、流媒体付费等等。基础设施制造了一种未来流量，不仅是货物或服务的流量，也是收入的流量。对未来收入的主张是一种金融资产，可以在当下提供出来。
en: Second, beyond the profits to be made from practices of sabotage and disruption, the financial goods that infrastructures bring into being enjoy a different relation to time from that of the other materials that infrastructures carry. The investment acquires its value not from the speed that brings things closer together, but from the delay that pushes things into the future. This quality arises from the fact that an infrastructure operates not only as a transportation device, but as a payment mechanism. It is an apparatus for the capture of future payments, in the form of freight charges, passenger fares, port fees, bridge and highway tolls, water rates, fuel costs, electricity bills, property rents, internet subscriptions, streaming payments, and more. The infrastructure manufactures a future flow, not simply of goods or services, but of revenues. The claim to those future revenues is a financial asset that can be made available in the present.

zh: 有几种方法可以把未来主张货币化，但从历史上看，最常见的方法是把基础设施项目组织为股份制公司。出售给投资者的公司股份，代表对流动所产生的未来费用或收入的主张。货物和服务往往可以通过更快交付而增值，但对未来收入流量的主张——我们将会看到——是通过延迟而获得价值的。
en: There are several ways to monetise the future claim, but, historically, the most common method has been to organise the infrastructure project as a joint-stock company. The shares in the company, sold to investors, represent claims on the future fees or revenues arising from the flows. While goods and services may often increase in value through faster delivery, the claim upon a future flow of revenue, as we will see, acquires its value through delay.

zh: 任何金融工具都可以因时间流逝而增值。事实上，仅仅通过延长时间就能增值的奇特能力，正是界定某种安排为金融资产的部分原因。这一特质使我们所谓的金融或资本对基础设施产生特殊依赖。基础设施项目是一种把时间流逝向前拉伸的装置。并非所有金融都由基础设施项目创造，但金融总是需要一种基础设施过程来建构被推迟的付款。基础设施是创造延迟的典范装置。
en: Any financial instrument can increase in value thanks to the passage of time. In fact, the strange ability to grow in value through the mere extension of time is part of what defines an arrangement as a financial asset. This quality gives what we call finance or capital a particular dependence on infrastructure. The infrastructure project is a device for stretching forwards the passing of time. Not all finance is created through infrastructure projects, but finance always requires an infrastructural process for the construction of postponed payments. Infrastructure is the paradigmatic apparatus for the creation of a delay.

zh: 要考察基础设施究竟如何被建造来创造延迟，我们必须首先重新排列我们思考大型技术项目以及一般资本的标准术语。基础设施塑造了我们对空间和时间、对物质性和
货币、对人类建构世界的理解，阻碍我们以不同方式思考。
en: To consider how exactly an infrastructure is built to create delays, we must first reorder the standard terms in which we think about large technical projects, and about capital in general. Infrastructure has shaped our conceptions of space and time, of materiality and
money, and of human world-making, impeding us from thinking differently.

zh: 如果我们倾向于从速度而非推迟、从流量加快而非延迟的角度思考基础设施，也许原因是，修建铁路、港口、公路系统、管道或公用事业网络，邀请我们把公开宣称的目的与成本分离。此类项目的提案和计划通常先呈现物质目的，再呈现货币安排。这种区分有助于支撑基础设施规划所特有的乐观，甚至傲慢。
一部分似乎物质、可触、可见，另一部分似乎金融、无形、难以想象。一个是目的，另一个只是手段。
en: If we tend to think of infrastructure in terms of speed rather than postponement, in terms of the quickening of flows rather than their delay, perhaps the reason is that the building of a rail line, port, road system, pipeline, or utility network invites us to separate the avowed purpose from the cost. The proposals and plans for such projects typically present the material purpose first, and the monetary arrangement second. This distinction helps underwrite the optimism, even the hubris, that is a characteristic of infrastructure planning.
One part seems material, tangible, and visible, the other financial, intangible, and difficult to visualise. One is the end, the other merely the means.

zh: 物质与金融、实体与货币、可见与无形之间的区分，部分是基础设施的效果。在实践中，基础设施项目的每个方面都是两者的混合。航运线路运送的货物或公用事业网络输送的能源，由物质、力、管理、价值和管理规定的各种组合构成，包括质量控制、价格机制和劳动力成本；同样，项目所产生的投资产品也依赖于生产此类“纸张”的材料和机制。
无论是印成股票凭证还是在计算机网络中生成，金融工具都涉及传输、登记、拍卖，尤其是未来付款强制执行的方法。而且，没有未来将为之付款的货物或服务，它们就无法存在。然而，尽管货物和金融都是物质与价值、有形与无形的混合体，基础设施建设似乎把它们分开，变出一个似乎划分为物质商品与货币、目的与手段、目的与价格、实体与金融、基础设施与其成本的世界。
en: The distinction between material and financial, real and monetary, visible and intangible, is partly an effect of infrastructure. In practice, each aspect of an infrastructure project is a mixture of both. The goods carried by a shipping line or the energy moved by a utility network are made up of various combinations of matter, force, management, value, and regulation, including quality controls, price mechanisms, and labour costs; likewise, the investment products that a project brings into being depend on the materials and mechanisms that produce such ‘paper’.

Whether printed as stock certificates or generated in computer networks, financial instruments involve methods of transmission, registration, auction, and, above all, enforcement of future payment. And they cannot exist without the future good or service for which that payment will be made. But, although both the goods and the finance are hybrids of matter and value, of the tangible and the intangible, the building of infrastructures appears to separate them, conjuring a world that seems divided into material goods versus money, ends versus means, purpose versus price, the real versus the financial, the infrastructure versus its cost.

zh: 在造成这个看似分裂的世界时，基础设施项目还赋予它一种等级秩序。新项目的推动者通常以物质需要而非金融机会向公众证明其合理性。将因新基础设施而更快流动的人员和物资，被呈现为必须满足的要求、生活的必需品、福祉的条件、一种改善，或如经济学家所称的福利增加或“增长”。金融——尽管暗中是唯一为增长而存在、其可能性本身就在于自身扩张的要素——则显得是次要的东西。资本借由这一托词，假装事后才到来，来使
需要得到满足。基础设施项目通过促成一种划分为实体与金融的世界效果，强化了实体或物质、生理需要和人类欲望的表面首要性，并把金融置于仆从、从属要素的位置，其存在只是为了帮助满足这些需要。它们产生一种形而上学效果——实体与金融的对立——这种效果在金融学和经济学理论中、在更广泛的社会科学中被复制。
en: In effecting this seemingly divided world, infrastructural projects also give it a hierarchy. The promoters of new projects usually justify them to the public by material needs, not financial opportunities. The movements and supplies that will flow faster thanks to new infrastructure are presented as a requirement to be met, a necessity for life, a condition of well-being, an improvement, or, as economists call it, an increase in welfare, or ‘growth’. The finance – although secretly the only element that actually exists in order to grow, the one factor whose very possibility lies in its own expansion – appears as something secondary. Claiming this alibi, capital pretends to arrive after the fact, to enable

needs to be met. In contributing to the effect of a world divided into the real and the financial, infrastructure projects reinforce the apparent primacy of the real or the material, of physical needs and human wants, and place finance as the servant, the subservient element existing only to help meet such needs. They generate a metaphysical effect, the real versus the financial, that is reproduced in theories of finance and economics, and in social science more generally.

zh: 资本的延迟
en: Delay of Capital

zh: 让我们颠倒这一优先顺序，至少暂时把金融问题放在首位——尽管我们稍后会重新表述这个问题。为什么资本似乎想要延迟？答案是，推迟使资本得以产生，并使其能够增殖。事实上，延迟——把某物推向未来却仍能控制它的技术能力——可以理解为资本的本质，以及资本那种被称为货币的流动形式的本质。
en: Let us reverse this order of priority and, at least provisionally, put the question of finance first – although we will later rephrase the question. Why does capital appear to want delay? The answer is that postponement brings capital into being and allows it to multiply. In fact, the delay – the technical ability to push something into the future yet continue to control it – can be understood as the very nature of capital, and of the liquid form of capital known as money.

zh: 按照惯例，如我们在
所述，正统经济学家通常把货币仅仅描述为便利交换、储存价值或记录账户的手段。然而，我们现在知道，或者说重新发现了这样一种知识：虽然货币可以发挥这些用途，但它大部分是以信用形式产生的。信用是一种会计机制——也就是说，既是一种会计，也是一种机制或技术装置。通过这一机制的运作，被许诺的未来收入在当下变得可用。如果债权人可以用这种付款承诺清偿其他债务，那么信用账户就作为货币运作。
en: By convention, as we noted in

, orthodox economists usually describe money as just a means to facilitate exchange, store value, or record accounts. However, we now know, or rather have rediscovered the knowledge, that while money can serve these purposes, for the most part it comes into being as credit. Credit is an accounting mechanism – that is, both an accounting, and a mechanism or technical apparatus. Through the working of the mechanism, promised future revenues are made accessible in the present. If the creditor can use that promise-to-pay to settle other debts, then the credit account operates as money.

zh: 虽然把货币理解为一种作为信用机制被创造的东西，而不只是储存价值或便利交换的手段，最近开始受到新的关注，但关于这个主题的许多写作都狭隘地集中于银行和其他金融机构研究。例如，虽然已有关于支持货币创造和运作的法律装置的重要研究，但很少有人探讨这里所呈现的信贷和资本创造的更广泛技术政治装置。
对货币的研究仍然着重于信任、社会关系和法律规制，而不把它作为一种技术政治关系来处理。甚至那些提出不应通过价值理论、而应把资本理解为一种权力关系的开创性文本，也往往依赖相当笼统的支配概念。
它们通常不从物质和技术层面考察特定的信用生产装置是如何建构的。
en: Although the understanding of money as something created as a credit mechanism, rather than simply a means of storing value or facilitating exchange, has recently begun to receive new attention, much of the writing on the topic is focused narrowly on the study of banking and other financial institutions. While there have been important studies of, for example, the legal apparatus that supports the creation and operation of money, there is little exploration of the wider technopolitical apparatuses of credit and capital creation presented here.

Money is still approached with an emphasis on trust, social relations, and legal regulation – not as a technopolitical relation. Even the seminal texts proposing that capital is to be understood not through value theory but as a power relation often rely on rather general notions of domination.
They do not usually consider in material and technical terms how a specific apparatus of credit production is constructed.

zh: 如果一种会计机制不仅指在纸上或电子方式进行的实践，而且指一种技术政治的物质装置，那么，许诺和攫取未来收入的装置在技术上和政治上越可靠，这一机制能向未来延伸得越远，创造信用货币的机会就越大。
en: If an accounting mechanism does not refer merely to practices carried out on paper, or electronically, but to a technopolitical, material apparatus, then the more reliable the apparatus for promising and capturing future revenue, both technically and politically, and the further the mechanism can be extended into the future, the greater the opportunity for the creation of credit money.

zh: 这就是理解基础设施与金融关系的方式：基础设施不只是恰好需要借入大量资金的物质投资。它们是创造大量信用货币的安排——这些安排像所有货币一样，通过一套延展的物质装置而产生。
en: This is how to understand the relationship between infrastructure and finance: infrastructures are not simply material investments that happen to require the borrowing of large amounts of money. They are the arrangements through which large amounts of credit money are created – arrangements that, like all money, come into being through an extended material apparatus.

zh: 从这个角度看，货币本身可以被视为一种基础设施。然而，我们必须谨慎对待这一类比。亚当·斯密在
中把金属货币比作允许商品流通的道路或铁路。他写道，货币就像“一条公路，它流通并把乡间所有牧草和谷物运往市场，但自身不生产一堆草或谷物”。他用这个隐喻解释银行发行纸币的作用：“银行审慎的操作，如果我可以允许自己使用这样一个大胆的隐喻，提供了一条穿越空中的马车轨道，使国家得以将其大部分公路变成良好的牧场和粮田。”
马车轨道是木制铁路，承载马拉货车，是斯密时代在苏格兰大规模修建的新基础设施，主要用于把煤从煤矿运到港口。斯密借用当代基础设施方案的这一隐喻，来应对 1760 年代和 1770 年代银行信用激增的问题，特别是 1772 年的一场银行危机：艾尔银行倒闭引发遍及苏格兰的“商业地震”，并使斯密自己的赞助人、英国最大的地主之一巴克卢公爵面临破产威胁。这场灾难使斯密推迟五年出版
，因为他重新思考银行创造信用的问题以及政府监管的必要性。
把信用货币描绘为“一条穿越空中的马车轨道”，从此一直是一个不充分的意象。金融不是由空气构成的，也不是实体货物的某种空灵对应物。它也不只是便利那些实体材料流通的手段。它自身就是一种物质基础设施，其存在
不仅是为了便利实体运动，而且本身就是要由基础设施增殖来便利的运动。
en: From this perspective, money can itself be approached as an infrastructure. However, we must be careful with this analogy. In

, Adam Smith compared metallic money to a road or railway, allowing the circulation of goods. Money, he wrote, is like ‘a highway, which, while it circulates and carries to market all the grass and corn of the country, produces itself not a single pile of either’. He used this metaphor to explain the role of banks in issuing paper money: ‘The judicious operations of banking, by providing, if I may be allowed so violent a metaphor, a sort of waggon-way through the air, enable the country to convert, as it were, a great part of its highways into good pastures and corn-fields.’

Waggon-ways were wooden railways carrying horse-drawn wagons, a new infrastructure built extensively in Scotland in Smith’s time, mainly to carry coal from collieries to harbours. Smith employed this metaphor from contemporary infrastructure schemes to grapple with the problem of the proliferation of bank credit in the 1760s and 1770s, and, in particular, a banking crisis in 1772 when the collapse of Ayr Bank caused a ‘commercial earthquake’ across Scotland and threatened Smith’s own benefactor, the Duke of Buccleuch, one of the largest landowners in Britain, with bankruptcy. The calamity caused Smith to delay the publication of
by five years as he rethought the problem of bank-created credit and the need for its regulation by government.

Portraying credit money as ‘a sort of waggon-way through the air’ has remained an inadequate image ever since. Finance is not built out of air, as some ethereal counterpart to real goods. And it is not merely a means to facilitate the circulation of those real materials. It is itself a material infrastructure, and one that exists
not merely to facilitate real movement, but as the movement to be facilitated by the proliferation of infrastructures.

zh: 如果建构一种攫取未来收入的装置创造了货币的可能，它也赋予货币一种奇特能力：显得能够“增长”。换言之，延迟的基础设施不仅产生货币的可能——即对某项未来资产的主张——而且产生资本的可能：一种看起来是货币自我扩张力量的东西。这种表象通过利用界定未来生产的两个特征的过程而产生：未来可以被推迟，其进程并不确定。
en: If the construction of an apparatus to capture revenue that lies in the future creates the possibility of money, it also gives money its peculiar ability of appearing to ‘grow’. In other words, the infrastructure of delay gives rise to the possibility not just of money, in the sense of a claim on a future asset, but of capital: of what appears as the self-expanding power of money. This appearance comes about through processes that take advantage of two features that define the making of the future: it is subject to delay, and its course is not certain.

zh: 那些设计并取得一系列未来付款主张之控制权的人——例如一项持久基础设施项目所许诺的付款，或者简单如未来销售的承诺收入——可能决定在当下出售这些主张或承诺的一部分，也许是为了清偿早先的债务或支持建造新的付款机器，或者只是为了兑现这种控制可能带来的意外收益。重复
中一个简单的例子：信用票据的持有者可以把这份付款承诺卖给第三方；这张票据代表另一个人的承诺，即在未来某一固定日期支付一定金额，以换取某种货物的交付。由于付款被推迟到未来，加上任何治理未来事件的安排都带有不确定性因素，这类未来收入主张通常可以以较低价格购得。这使未来收入可以按折扣获得。
en: Those who engineer and acquire control of a set of claims on future payments, such as those promised by a durable infrastructural project, but also something as simple as the promised income from a future sale, may decide to sell a part of those claims or promises in the present, perhaps to settle earlier debts or to support the building of new payment machines; or simply to realise the windfall to which such control may give rise. To repeat a straightforward instance from

, the owner of a credit note – a promise from someone else to pay a certain sum on a fixed day in the future, in exchange for the delivery of a certain good – might sell that promise-of-payment to a third party. Due to the postponement of the payment into the future, and the element of uncertainty that attaches to any arrangement for governing prospective events, such claims to future revenue can usually be purchased at a reduced price. This makes the future income available at a discount.

zh: 让我们简要重述这一过程如何运作。一年后可得的一笔 100 美元付款主张，现在也许可以按折扣价购买，比如 10% 的折扣，即 90 美元。如果许诺付款的日期可以被推得更远，折扣可以在收入被推迟的每一年复合，成倍放大其效果。因此，七年后的一笔 100 美元收入主张，按同样的年折扣率，现在也许能以约 50 美元购得。
只要延迟装置在政治上和技术上可靠，剩余不确定性可以得到管理，这种安排就允许投资者以 50 美元的价格购买 100 美元收入的主张。换言之，在 10% 的折扣率下，50 美元可以在七年内显得规模翻倍，而投资者乃至资金本身都无需付出任何努力。（资金并不代表建造延迟装置的成本，即使部分收入可能用于支付这些成本；它们代表的是其未来
收入的折价购买价格。）这样，延迟机制就允许创造信用货币，并赋予它那种奇特的增长能力。
en: Let us recount out briefly how this process works. The claim to a payment of $100 that will be available one year from now might be purchased in the present at a discount, say of 10 per cent, or for the price of $90. If the date of the promised payment can be pushed further into the future, the discount can be compounded each year that the revenue is postponed, multiplying its effect. Thus the claim to a revenue of $100 in seven years’ time might be purchased in the present, at the same annual discount rate, for about $50.

Provided the apparatus of postponement is politically and technically reliable and the residual uncertainty can be managed, this arrangement allows an investor to purchase the claim to an income of $100 at the price of $50. In other words, at a discount rate of 10 per cent, the sum of $50 can appear to double in size in seven years, through no effort on the part of the investor, or even of the funds themselves. (The funds do not represent the cost of building the apparatus of postponement, even if some of the income may be used to defray those costs; rather, they represent the discounted purchase price of its future
revenues.) In this way, the mechanism of delay allows the creation of credit money and endows it with its curious capacity to grow.

zh: 大多数投资者以及他们所属的公众，把这种七年间从 50 美元到 100 美元的转变视为货币“赚取利息”的力量。可以说，他们是从望远镜的另一端看问题，从当下凝视未来。从未来某个人的角度回望，一项资产规模缩小了，因为 100 美元收入的价值被减至 50 美元。但如果反过来看，从当下那一刻向前看，50 美元数额已经扩大了一倍。利息概念使这种增加显得是货币的自然属性。这种表象把注意力从必须完成的基础设施工作——以及必须组织的权力——上转移开，这些工作和权力用于建造和治理一套可靠的延迟、收入攫取和信用创造装置。
en: Most investors, and the wider public to which they belong, come to think of this transformation of $50 into $100 over a period of seven years as the power of money to ‘earn interest’. They see it, as it were, through the other end of the telescope, staring at the future from the present. From the perspective of a person in the future, looking back, an asset was shrunken in size, because an income of $100 was reduced in value to $50. But, seen in reverse, from that present moment looking forwards, the sum of $50 has enlarged to become double the size. The concept of interest makes the increase appear as a natural property of money. This appearance diverts attention from the infrastructural work that must be done – and the powers that must be organised – to build and govern a reliable apparatus of postponement, revenue capture, and credit creation.

zh: 从历史上看，如我们所见，计算未来收入价值与其当下价格之间差额的做法被称为“贴现”，这个术语在金融界仍然常用。今天看起来像投资的“增长”，更有用的理解方式——正如贴现一词所暗示的——是未来的“缩减”。付款可以按其最终价值的一小部分从未来榨取。但这取决于建造使未来可用的机制。一定量货币看似能使自身规模翻倍的能力，并不依赖货币的任何物理膨胀力量。它是一套技术政治装置的后果，这套装置制造阻塞、中断和缩减。我们所谓的资本，或具有增长力量的货币，就是这种建造和治理付款之可靠推迟与贴现的安排。
en: Historically, the practice of calculating the difference between the value of a future revenue and its price in the present was known, as we have seen, as ‘discounting’, a term still commonly used in the world of finance. What today appears as the ‘growth’ of an investment can more usefully be understood, as the term discounting suggests, as the ‘reduction’ of the future. Payments can be extracted from the future at a fraction of their eventual value. But this depends on building the mechanism that makes that future available. The ability of a certain quantity of money to apparently double its size does not rest on any power of physical expansion of money. It is a consequence of a technopolitical apparatus that creates an obstruction, interruption, and shrinkage. What we call capital, or money with the power to grow, is this kind of arrangement for building and governing the reliable postponement and discounting of payments.

zh: 先前问资本为什么
想要延迟时，“显得”一词很重要。但最好重新表述问题。资本在这里可能显得是行动者，寻求使其能够扩张的可靠推迟形式。然而，既然资本是延迟过程的
，把它仅仅视为这些过程的行动者就说不通了。资本不是从过去储存下来、寻求向未来扩张的东西。它是从未来获得的，途径是建造付款装置和强制执行机制，使预期收入能够在当下按折扣可靠地获得。
en: In asking earlier why capital

to want a delay, the term ‘appearance’ was important. But it is better to rephrase the terms of the question. Capital may appear here as the agent, seeking the forms of reliable postponement that allow it to expand. However, since capital is the

of the processes of delay, it does not make sense to consider it simply as the agent of those processes. Capital is not something stored up from the past, seeking expansion into the future. It is acquired from the future, through the building of payment devices and enforcement mechanisms that make prospective income reliably available at a discount in the present.

zh: 从未来获得的收入，主要由
基础设施的使用者支付。在以股份制公司组织的基础设施项目中，购买公司股份的人确立了对公司部分利润的永久主张。此后，股东的主张成为使用和运营基础设施者必须承担的负担。它是加在货物运输费、乘客票价、水费和电费、服务订阅费之上的一项成本，也是强加在管理和操作这一过程者工资上的一笔开支。这些票价、费用、费率和工资不仅承担运营和维护基础设施的成本，还承担事先卖给股东的那项额外主张。
en: The revenue acquired from the future is paid largely by the users of

the infrastructure. In the case of an infrastructure project organised as a joint-stock company, those who purchase shares in the company establish a perpetual claim on a portion of the company’s profits. Going forwards, the claim of the shareholder becomes a burden to be carried by those who use and run the infrastructure. It is a cost added to charges for shipping goods, or the fares paid by passengers, or the rates charged for water and electricity, or the fees for subscribing to a service, and it is an expense imposed on the wages of those who manage and operate the process. Those fares, fees, rates, and wages carry not only the cost of operating and maintaining the infrastructure, but the additional claim sold in advance to the shareholders.

zh: 耐久
en: The Durable

zh: 通过被推迟付款的主张创造信用货币，本身并非新近的做法。然而，正如

所探讨的，在更早的世纪里，延迟的基础设施并非由钢铁、混凝土和石料、铜和光纤电缆，或今天通常用于建造持久未来付款攫取装置的其他材料构成。延迟不那么持久。在帝国时代之前，其最常见的装置是作物周期：下一季收获的许诺构成了可据以创造信用的未来。如我们所述，另一种延迟可以由延展的商业关系构成。大型贸易网络——例如横跨中世纪印度—伊斯兰世界及其以外的网络——允许建立信用票据或汇票等信贷安排。这些创造信用并予以贴现的技术后来扩展到欧洲。
作为为未来货物付款、在若干周或数月内交付的承诺，票据或汇票可以作为货币运作。它成为中世纪和近代早期世界最广泛使用的信贷和资本创造体系。
en: The creation of credit money through claims to delayed payments is not in itself a recent practice. However, as

explored, in earlier centuries the infrastructures of delay were not built of iron and steel, concrete and masonry, copper and fibre-optical cabling, or the other materials typically used today to build durable apparatuses for the capture of future payments. Delay was less durable. Its most common apparatus before the imperial age was the crop cycle, in which the promise of next season’s harvest constituted the future for which credit could be created. Another kind of delay, as we noted, could be built from extended commercial relations. Large trading networks, such as those organised across the medieval Indo-Islamic world and beyond, allowed the building of credit arrangements such as the promissory note or bill of exchange. These techniques of creating credit and discounting it were later extended to Europe.

As a promise to pay for future goods, due for delivery within a certain number of weeks or months, the note or bill could function as money. It became the most widely used system of credit and capital creation across the medieval and early modern world.

zh: 随着欧洲人把中东—亚洲贸易从陆路和沿海路线改道至迂回的海路，制造信用的更大机会出现了。建造可靠的海船、军事贸易站和补给点，使欧洲人得以逐渐主导这一贸易。回顾
提出的观点：在铁路时代之前，武装帆船及其设防航线成为产生和贴现未来收入的最复杂、最昂贵的装置。“一艘船是一台极其
复杂的机器，或者更确切地说，是大多数已知机器的组合，”法国造船师皮埃尔·福尔费在 1788 年写道。
正如一位造船学史学家所指出的，武装帆船“结合了船体和桅杆的厚重木质结构，令人眼花缭乱的支撑桅杆的固定索具，数百条控制横桁和帆的绳索与滑轮，起锚用的绞盘，转动舵的舵柄和舵轮，舱底泵等等”。
这种强度与可控性的结合，构成了一种足够可靠、足够灵活、武装足够充分的装置，能够在远离贸易项目资助者的地方远程运作，通过殖民地贸易的新时间滞后，创造出有利可图的收入“延迟”。组织航运的荷兰和英国商人创立了第一批股份制公司，通过它们，未来收入的股份可以按折扣买卖。同样的信用创造方法扩展到欧洲的北大西洋和加勒比殖民地，扩展到被奴役人口的贸易及其生产的糖、烟草和其他货物。
en: Larger opportunities to manufacture credit arose with the European diversion of Middle Eastern–Asian trade from overland and coastal routes to circuitous seaborne passages. The building of reliable, oceangoing ships and military trading posts and provisioning points enabled Europeans to gradually dominate this trade. To recall a point made in
, before the age of railways, the armed sailing ship and its fortified route became the most complex and expensive apparatus for generating and discounting future revenue. ‘A vessel is an extremely
composite machine, or rather it is a combination of most known machines’, wrote the French shipbuilder Pierre Forfait in 1788.

As a historian of naval architecture notes, armed sailing ships ‘combined the heavy wooden construction of the hull and masts with a dizzying array of standing rigging to support the masts, hundreds of lines and blocks to control the yardarms and sails, capstans for hauling up the anchors, tillers and wheels to turn the rudder, bilge pumps, and such’.

This combination of strength and controllability formed an apparatus that was reliable enough, manoeuvrable enough, and sufficiently armed to operate at a great distance, remote from those who sponsored the trading venture, creating a profitable ‘delay’ in revenue, via the new time lag of colonial trade. The Dutch and English merchants who organised the shipping created the first joint-stock companies, through which shares in prospective revenues could be bought and sold at a discount. The same methods of credit creation were extended to Europe’s North Atlantic and Caribbean colonies, and to the trade in enslaved populations and the sugar, tobacco, and other goods they produced.

zh: 为了支持和扩大这种殖民地贸易以及自身收入，欧洲国家建立海军并从事长期战争。殖民战争产生了一种更大的延期付款体系：商人预支信贷，为军事力量的部署提供资金。这种信贷供给形成了更新、更可靠的付款延迟，即所谓的国债，进而促成了国家货币的创造。这些货币后来被错误地视为货币的本质。随着政府发展更广泛的征税方式为这些付款融资，并配套建立扣押货物和因债务监禁的权力，国家权力的持久性以及日益增强的稳定性和规模，促成了新规模的资本创造。
en: To support and expand this colonial trade, and their own revenues, European states built naval forces and engaged in protracted wars. Colonial warfare gave rise to a larger system of delayed payment, the credit advanced by merchants to fund the deployment of military force. This provision of credit formed the new and more reliable payment delays known as national debt, which led, in turn, to the creation of national currencies. These currencies would mistakenly come to be thought of as the very essence of money. As governments developed the more extensive modes of taxation required to finance these payments, and the accompanying powers of seizure of goods and imprisonment for debt, the longevity and increasing stability and scale of state power gave rise to capital creation on a new scale.

zh: 在现代、殖民规模的贸易和战争发展之前，通过未来金融贴现获利，受到创造可靠延迟收入之过程的有限持续时间和范围的制约。所能创造的延迟一般以作物周期和贸易路线所规定的月数来衡量，而不是以年或十年计，因此所谓“增长”的可能性受到限制。对未来遥远收入的索取主张价值不大。它们还受到互惠、义务、伦理提升和慷慨等实践的制约——这些无疑以各种组合构成所有道德传统的特征，但也许在某些大商业中心尤为显著，比如
伊斯兰世界的中心——这些实践限制了非劳动所得的榨取和债务的强制执行。地产可以保证长期收入，但由于对未来收入的权利通常依赖于对历史久远的占有权的主张，或依赖保护的保证（奴隶种植园除外），它们不容易被出售给陌生人。
没有现成机制可以在当下交易这类未来份额。除了现代国家本身以及与其共同演化的殖民公司和种植园之外，没有任何装置能够产生足够可靠的收入，使其可以在数年内有利可图地延迟，又具有足够流动性，可以在当下按折扣交易。
en: Prior to the development of modern, colonial-scale trade and warfare, profiting through financial discounting of the future was constrained by the limited duration and extent of the processes that created a reliably delayed income. The delays that could be created were generally measured in the months laid out by crop cycles and trade routes, not in years or decades, so were restricted in the possibility of so-called ‘growth’. There was little value to a claim to revenue that lay far in the future. They were also constrained by practices of reciprocity, obligation, ethical improvement, and generosity – characteristic no doubt of all moral traditions in various combinations, but especially marked, perhaps, in some of the centres of great commerce, such as

those of the Islamic world – that placed limits on the extraction of unearned income and the enforcement of debt. Landed estates might guarantee long-term income, but since the rights to that future revenue typically depended (with the exception of slave plantations) on claims to ancient possession, or on guarantees of protection, they could not easily be sold to strangers.

There was no readily available mechanism for trading shares in such futures in the present. Apart from the modern state itself, and the colonising corporations and plantations through which it coevolved, there was no apparatus for generating revenue that was reliable enough that it might be profitably delayed over several years, and liquid enough to trade at a discount in the present.

zh: 正如我们在

所探讨并在此可以概括的，资本创造对殖民扩张和战争、对奴役劳动和其他形式暴力的依赖，带来了中断风险。对这种中断的回应，造成了后来对延迟和推迟在资本创造中作用的误解，这种误解至今仍广泛流行。大约从 1775 年到 1815 年的约四十年间，整个通过远距离殖民地贸易创造信用的体系，因南亚、北美、奥斯曼帝国和加勒比地区的政治变革，随后又因遍及欧洲和近东的战争，而中断并几乎停顿。错乱的信贷和资本创造模式通过一个新的绕道得到重组：穿过兰开夏郡的水力棉纺厂。这个绕道利用并迅速发展了一种新的信用体系，它与时间性有着不同的关系。以往长期沿袭的做法，是商人把货物借给将其加工成纺织品的人；如今则由工人提供信用：工人把劳动借给那些转而建造工厂的商人。
这个绕道是艰苦的劳动，不仅对数万名被迫进入工厂劳动的人如此，对丧失了通过垄断基础设施创造财富这一更古老、更简便方法的商人也是如此。几十年内，建造垄断性基础设施的新机会出现了。但在此期间，马克思阅读了英国工厂视察员的报告，并从中得出一种基于这台新时间机器——工厂——的资本理论。
en: As we explored in

, and can summarise here, this dependence of capital creation on colonial expansion and warfare, and on enslaved labour and other forms of violence, brought risks of disruption. The response to this disruption created what became a misunderstanding of the role of delay and postponement in the creation of capital, a misunderstanding that still prevails widely today. Over roughly four decades from about 1775 to 1815, the entire system of credit creation through long-distance colonial trade was disrupted and almost brought to a halt by political transformations in South Asia, North America, the Ottoman Empire, and the Caribbean, and then by war across Europe and the Near East. Dislocated patterns of credit and capital creation were reorganised by means of a new detour: through the water-driven cotton mills of Lancashire. The detour took advantage of, and rapidly developed, a new credit system, one with a different relation to temporality. Rather than the long-standing practice of merchants loaning goods to those who made them into textiles, the credit was extended by workers, who loaned their labour to the merchants, now building mills.

This detour was hard work, not only for the tens of thousands forced into factory labour, but for the merchants deprived of the older and easier method of creating wealth through the monopoly of infrastructures. Within a few decades, new opportunities for building monopolistic infrastructure emerged. But, in the meantime, Marx had read the reports of English factory inspectors and derived from them a theory of capital based on this new time machine, the factory.

zh: 从十九世纪后期起，可以建造持久得多、用于攫取未来的装置。其中大多数采取基础设施项目的形式。其典型是修建长途
铁路。这类大型、长期建设项目为信用创造提供了新机会。
en: From the later nineteenth century, much more durable apparatuses for capturing the future could be built. Most of these took the form of infrastructure projects. They were typified by the building of long-distance
railways. Such large, long-term construction projects offered new opportunities for the creation of credit.

zh: 新基础设施项目的两个特征，促成了更大幅度的延迟。第一，正如我们在

所述，与其他攫取收入的手段相比，即使在今天，基础设施也异常耐久。铁路、水坝、港口、管道、公路、输电线、通信网络和数据中心由混凝土、钢铁、铜、热塑性塑料和其他耐久材料建成。技术韧性和耐久性是这类基础设施安排的构成特征。按照设计，它们必须比其所引导和便利流动的瞬态货物、车辆、液体、数据和人员更耐久。基础设施运载的材料往往打算在数月、数日、数分钟或更短时间内消耗掉，本身几乎不产生长期收入流；而基础设施的寿命通常以年或十年计。可以按折扣购买的未来收入，部分是这种必要差异的产物：意在消耗的供应品或流具有可分解性，而承载它们流动的装置具有不可分解性。
en: Two features of the new infrastructure projects contributed to making possible the much larger postponement of time. First, as we noted in

, compared with other means of capturing revenue, even today, infrastructures are unusually durable. Railways, dams, ports, pipelines, highways, power lines, communication networks, and data centres are built of concrete, steel, copper, thermoplastics, and other resilient materials. Technical resilience and durability are constituent features of such infrastructure arrangements. By design they must be more resilient than the transient goods, vehicles, liquids, data, and persons whose flow they channel and enable. While the materials carried by infrastructures are often intended to be consumed within months, days, minutes, or less, creating in themselves little in the way of long-term revenue streams, the life of infrastructure is typically measured in years or decades. The future revenue that can be purchased at a discount is, in part, the product of this necessary difference between the decomposability of supplies or streams intended to be consumed and the non-decomposing quality of the apparatus through which they flow.

zh: 第二，与许多其他攫取收入的手段相比，基础设施通常还以另一种耐久性建造：一种政治和法律保障。作为简略说法，它们可以被描述为垄断。但这个词简化了保障的不同要素。作为安排和控制流动的装置，基础设施往往固定在原地、向外建成，是一种不动产（在某些用法中，基础设施几乎成为任何大于建筑的实体结构的标签）。像所有不动产一样，与可移动货物相对，这种结构具有垄断性，排他地占据空间，阻止其他使用者进入该空间，或向他们收费。收费可以小到向公用事业公司支付的家庭用水费，也可以大到集装箱船或油轮在“长赐号”事故发生前后，通行苏伊士运河所需支付的 50 万至 80 万美元通行费。
即使是数字基础设施也垄断空间，不仅通过把数字平台转变为具有产权归属的资产而在比喻和法律意义上如此，还通过占据关键地理位置或对电力供应、跨洋电缆和其他必需品的优先获取权来垄断空间。
en: Second, more than many other means of capturing revenues, infrastructures are typically built with another kind of durability, a form of political and legal guarantee. As a shorthand, they can be described as monopolies. But that term simplifies the different elements of the guarantee. As an apparatus for the ordering and control of flows, an infrastructure tends to be fixed in place, built out, a form of real estate (in some uses, infrastructure becomes the label for almost any material structure larger than a building). Like all real property, in contrast to movable goods, the structure is monopolising, occupying space exclusively, blocking other users from that space, or charging them for its use. The charge can be as minor as the household rates paid to a utility company for the supply of domestic water, or as large as the $500,000 to $800,000 transit fee that a container ship or oil tanker was paying, at the time of the Ever Given disaster, to navigate through the Suez Canal.

Even digital infrastructures monopolise space, not only figuratively and legally, through transforming digital platforms into propertied assets, but by occupying key geographical locations or privileged access to electricity supplies, transoceanic cables, and other requirements.

zh: 此外，由于基础设施规模庞大、物质上延展，建造它们通常涉及政府权力和强制力量。水坝、港口、铁路、公路、电站
和通信线路通常需要当局授予或批准的特许权，授予并强制执行对陆路、河道、港口、输电走廊或通信节点的排他控制。这不只是政府授予垄断权的问题。在现代国家时代，地方和国家政府的权力本身，都是通过法律体系、立法委员会、市政和港口当局以及其他声称拥有建造、许可、治安管理和管理基础设施之权力的机构的发展而出现的。
政府和基础设施作为相互依赖、空间界定的权力形式共同演化，在信用创造的技术政治工作中合作。
en: Moreover, since infrastructures are large, materially extended arrangements, building them usually involves powers of government and forces of coercion. Dams, ports, railroads, highways, power stations,

and communication lines typically require a concession or authorisation from an authority, awarding and enforcing exclusive control of a land route, river channel, harbour, transmission corridor, or communication node. This is not simply a question of governments granting monopoly rights. The very powers of government, in the era of the modern state, both local and national, emerged through the development of legal systems, legislative committees, municipal and port authorities, and other bodies that claimed powers to build, license, police, and manage infrastructure.
Government and infrastructure coevolved as interdependent forms of spatially defined power, collaborating in the technopolitical work of credit creation.

zh: 政府和基础设施的共同演化，使某些基础设施场址可以作为改变或中止普通政府权力的区域运作。殖民贸易公司建立的设防飞地是早期例子，黎凡特地区由欧洲商人各个“民族”居住的“商馆”或贸易站也是如此。
劳伦·本顿表明，帝国管辖权和主权通过“走廊”（如河流和道路网络）和“飞地”（如定居点和前哨）不均衡地扩张。
如今，正如黛博拉·考恩所指出的，这些“物流空间”继续例证着有组织暴力的强化，供应链的“致命生活”在那里集中。
当今最常见的例子是名称奇特的“自由区”。它可能是港口区域或类似飞地，通常靠近国际边界并与运输路线相连，由独立于国内法的当局授权并便利货物、资本、治安力量和劳动力的流动。该区域通常免征国家税和消费税，中止国家劳动法和环境立法的适用，并运营自己的安全和监控系统。
在埃及，苏伊士运河出口区提供了一个典型例子。在海湾部分地区，包括巴林和迪拜，国家的大量财富和权力都围绕创设这类区域而组织起来。
en: The coevolution of government and infrastructure allowed certain infrastructure sites to operate as zones in which ordinary government power is modified or suspended. The fortified enclaves created by colonial trading companies were an early example of this, as were the ‘factories’ or trading stations populated by the various ‘nations’ of European merchants in the Levant.
Lauren Benton shows that imperial jurisdiction and sovereignty expanded unevenly through ‘corridors’, such as river and road networks, and ‘enclaves’, such as settlements and outposts.
Today, as Deborah Cowen notes, these ‘logistics spaces’ continue to exemplify an intensification of organised violence, where the ‘deadly life’ of supply chains is concentrated.

The most common example today is the curiously named ‘free zone’. This might be a port area or similar enclave, typically close to an international border and connected to transportation routes, in which an authority independent of domestic law authorises and facilitates the movement of goods, capital, policing, and labour. The zone is typically exempt from national taxes and excise duties, suspends the application of national labour laws and environmental legislation, and operates its own security and surveillance systems.

In Egypt, the Suez Canal Export Zone provides a typical example. In some parts of the Gulf, including Bahrain and Dubai, much of the wealth and power of the state has been organised around the creation of such zones.

zh: 基础设施还有第三个增强其耐久性的特征：它们成为技术、经济和商业报道的对象，受到衡量、制表、压力测试、监测和指数化。
讨论的普尔的
就是这类实践的显著例子。这种对基础设施的报道、衡量和监测，要求并鼓励发展凯勒·伊斯特林所谓的“国家之外的治理术”：标准、可重复的公式
和协议，它们构成治理空间的“操作系统”，尤其是看似处于国家直接治理之外的空间，例如自由区以及我们提到的、由大型基础设施促成和鼓励的其他设防例外场址。
en: There is a third feature of infrastructures that enhances their durability: they become the object of technical, economic, and business reporting, which measures, tabulates, stress-tests, monitors, and indexes. Poor’s
, discussed in

, was a notable example of such practices. This reporting, measuring, and monitoring of infrastructure requires and encourages the development of what Keller Easterling terms ‘extrastatecraft’: standards, repeatable formulas,

and protocols which form the ‘operating system’ for the governing of space, especially spaces seemingly outside the direct government of the state, such as free zones and other fortified and exceptional sites that, as we noted, large infrastructures enable and encourage.

zh: 流动
en: The Liquid

zh: 然而，无论是技术耐久性还是政治耐久性，都只是从未来获利之力量扩张的一个方面。延长控制收入的时间跨度本身，并不能成为大量预期收益的来源。毕竟，即使古人也能随着时间推移建造大型、持久的物质结构和政治秩序。把时间组织为大规模创造资本的手段，需要耐久性与其反面相结合：流动性。
en: Durability, however, both technical and political, is only one aspect of the expanding power to profit from the future. Extending the length of time over which revenue is controlled cannot become the source of large prospective gain by itself. After all, even the ancients, over time, could build large, enduring material structures and political orders. The organisation of time as a means of creating capital on a large scale requires the combination of durability with its obverse: liquidity.

zh: 只有当对未来付款的主张成为一种可以迅速进入流通的权利——一种对财产的法律主张——时，未来付款才能成为不断扩张的利润、差额收益的来源。未来收入主张的所有者必须能够随时将其转让给另一个所有者。这种可转让性首先使信用创造成为可能，开启了按折扣购买的可能，从而带来贴现利润。
en: Future payments can become a source of expanding profit, of differential gain, only when the claim to them becomes a right – a legal claim to property – that can be quickly put in motion. The owner of the claim on future revenue must be able to readily transfer it to another owner. This transferability allows the creation of credit in the first place, setting up the possibility of purchase at a discount and thus the profit from discounting.

zh: 因此，用于攫取未来付款的持久装置的发展，在每个阶段都伴随着一个对应过程的发展：一种把对未来主张转化为可立即交换之物的机制。持久基础设施所产生的金融“票据”形式——票据、债券、股份、衍生品和其他货币工具——是硬化、耐久的攫取装置的轻质“液态”对应物。
en: So, the development of durable apparatuses for capturing future payments is accompanied at every stage by the development of a counterpart process: a mechanism for converting claims on the future into something immediately exchangeable. The forms of financial ‘paper’ to which durable infrastructures give rise – bills, bonds, shares, derivatives, and other kinds of monetary instrument – are the lightweight, ‘liquid’ corollary of the hardened, resilient apparatuses of capture.

zh: 这些轻质法律装置，无论以纸质还是电子形式，都执行一种转译行为，把基础设施攫取未来收入的所有不同模式转化为同一种东西：信用货币。使对未来主张可转译、从而可立即从一个所有者转让给另一个所有者并可贴现，不只是给它们标上数字或价格的问题。股票凭证或汇票可能有面值，但其有效价值只能通过建立定价机制来确定，换言之，通过建立被称为“市场”的金融装置来确定。基础设施的建设伴随着货币市场的建设，也因货币市场而成为可能。殖民时代的军事化航线和
战争，过去一个半世纪的运输、能源、水利和通信基础设施，以及最近几十年的数字通路和平台，都促进了创造、交换和贴现信用货币之新制度的形成。
en: These lightweight legal devices, whether in paper or electronic form, carry out an act of translation, converting all the different modes of infrastructural capture of future revenue into instances of the same thing: credit money. Making claims on the future translatable, and thus instantly transferable from one owner to another, and discountable, is not simply a matter of marking them with a number, or a price. A stock certificate or bill of exchange may have a face value, but its effective value can only be established by building a pricing mechanism, or, in other words, the financial apparatus known as a ‘market’. The building of infrastructures was accompanied, and made possible, by the building of money markets. The militarised shipping routes and warfare of

the colonial age, the transportation, energy, hydraulic, and communication infrastructures of the last century and a half, and the digital pathways and platforms of the most recent decades each facilitated the forming of new institutions for creating, exchanging, and discounting credit money.

zh: 流动性的创造还需要更多东西。货币装置的轻质特性使它们可以大量捆绑在一起。部分正是这种捆绑，使银行家能够提前以“折扣”提供任何一项未来主张。银行在当下发行的信用货币，由银行借以保证自身信用的未来付款的数量和多样性来担保。

与此同时，正如杰弗里·英厄姆所指出的，资本主义货币的独特之处在于一种机制，它把这些私人债务—信用契约转化为“货币”——一种由国家承认并实施的普遍许诺（通过接受以货币纳税）。这通过另一种“差异”的生产而发生：私人银行与政府货币当局或中央银行之间，以及政府与其债权人（债券持有人）和债务人（纳税人）之间的差异。中央银行用国家货币购买银行的私人债务——付款承诺。结果，私人信用货币被货币化，并变得在任何地方都可接受。这最初发生在英格兰银行贴现地方银行的票据之时。国家并不“控制”这一过程，而是试图加以规制。
en: This creation of liquidity requires something more. The lightweight quality of the monetary devices allows them to be bundled together in large quantities. It is, in part, this bundling that enables bankers to make any one claim on the future available in advance, at a ‘discount’. The credit money issued by banks in the present is secured by the sheer quantity and variety of future payments with which the bank guarantees its credit.

Simultaneously, as Geoffrey Ingham points out, capitalist money is distinctive in the mechanism that converts these private debt-credit contracts into ‘money’ – a universal promise, recognised and implemented by the state (via its acceptance for the payment of taxes). This happens through another production of ‘difference’, between private banks and a government monetary authority or central bank, and between the government and its creditors (bondholders) and debtors (taxpayers). The central bank purchases the private debts of banks – promises to pay – with state money. As a result, private credit money is monetised, and made acceptable anywhere. This first happened when the Bank of England discounted the bills of country banks. The state does not ‘control’ this but attempts to regulate it.

zh: 十九世纪后期的大型碳燃料基础设施项目，帮助促成了现代商业银行业的形成；商业银行负责组织由新基础设施耐久性所促成的流动性和信用机制。如我们所见，它们还刺激了另一种通过贴现未来收益生产信贷的制度发展：股东所有的公司。此后一百五十年间，公司成为组织财富积累和集中也许最有效的安排。正是铁路的建设——尤其是十九世纪后期的横贯大陆铁路和其他长途殖民地铁路——催生了这种组织资本的新方式。铁路公司的股票是伦敦、纽约和其他金融中心不断扩张的证券交易所中最常见的投资品。此前，股份只代表对企业当前物质资产的部分所有权。在大型基础设施的新时代，股份被转变为对基础设施可靠地置于未来的收入的所有权主张。
en: The great carbon-fuelled infrastructure projects of the later nineteenth century helped create modern commercial banking, as organisers of the liquidity and credit mechanisms facilitated by the durability of the new infrastructures. They also spurred, as we have seen, the development of another institution for the production of credit via the discounting of future earnings: the shareholder-owned corporation. Over the following 150 years, the corporation became perhaps the most effective arrangement for organising the accumulation and concentration of wealth. It was the building of railways, especially the transcontinental and other long-distance colonial lines of the later nineteenth century, that gave rise to this new way of organising capital. Shares of railway companies were the most common investment traded on the expanding stock exchanges of London, New York, and other financial centres. Previously, shares represented simply the part ownership of the current material assets of a business. In the new age of large infrastructure, shares were transformed into the ownership claim on the revenues that infrastructures placed reliably in the future.

zh: 能够获得信贷的人可以按折扣购买未来收入的一份——例如来自铁路线路开发商的收入。开发商将实现即时利润，实际上往往是一笔巨大的意外之财，因为未来收入可能值建设基础设施成本的许多倍。购买股份的投资者将获得未来收入，其贴现反映了该收入在五年、十年或五十年内不可得的事实。
en: Those with access to credit could purchase a share of the future revenue – from the developers of a railway line, for example – at a discount. The developers would realise an immediate profit, in fact often a great windfall, since the future revenues might be worth many times the cost of building the infrastructure. The share-buying investor would acquire the future revenue, discounted to reflect the fact that the revenue would not be available for five, ten, or fifty years.

zh: 大型基础设施项目不是推迟和攫取未来的唯一装置。这一过程逐渐采取许多其他形式，包括其他大型股东所有的产业、投机性房地产和抵押贷款融资的发展、各种消费信贷形式，以及最终电子平台的建造和控制，随着资产化蔓延到越来越多的生活领域。
但在更早的几十年里，从十九世纪后期开始，铁路、初生的石油工业和其他大型基础设施公司开创了这些建构和攫取未来的形式，并成为最大的范例；它们继续例证着基础设施以其变化的形式，如何让我们理解以未来为代价的生活方式。
en: Large infrastructure projects were not the only apparatus for the postponement and capture of the future. The process gradually took many other forms, including other large shareholder-owned industries, speculative real estate and the development of mortgage financing, forms of consumer credit, and eventually the building and control of electronic platforms, as assetisation spread into more and more areas of life.

But, in earlier decades, starting in the later nineteenth century, railways, the nascent oil industry, and other large infrastructure firms pioneered these forms of constructing and capturing the future and were the largest examples; they continue to exemplify many of the ways in which infrastructure, in its changing forms, allows us to understand the modes of living at the expense of the future.

zh: 法律体系帮助赋予未来收入主张以耐久性和流动性，但所做的还不止这些。在裁决对收入流的相互竞争的主张时——例如在股东、债权人和享有工资或退休金债权者之间——它确立优先顺序。在多数法域，法律逐渐把企业股份视为一种财产形式，赋予其持有人不仅对公司实物资产的权利，还有对未来收入的所有权主张。
en: The legal system helps to give claims to future revenue both their durability and their liquidity, but also does more. In adjudicating among rival claims to a stream of income, for example among those who own shares, those who are owed debts, and those who are owed wages or retirement pensions, it establishes priorities. In most jurisdictions, the law came to treat shares in a business venture as a form of property, giving their holders not only rights over the physical assets of a company but an ownership claim to revenue in the future.

zh: 虽然基础设施许诺耐久性，但在实践中，它很少可能享有这种许诺所暗示的稳定性。学者们过去认为，基础设施的特质之一是其不可见性。它通常在后台或地下运作，使大多数服务使用者对其运转无所察觉。与许多技术史一样，这种论述是从成功项目的立场、而非从技术系统设计者面对不确定结果时的立场写成的。
更好的看法是，基础设施并非不可见，而是一种检测、报道和核算过程的组织，试图管理各种可见性形式。每一种技术装置都需要维护和修理，都可能发生故障、衰败和失效。
en: While an infrastructure promises durability, in practice, it is seldom likely to enjoy the stability that the promise might imply. Scholars used to argue that one of the qualities of infrastructure was its invisibility. It typically operates in the background, or below ground, keeping most users of its services unaware of its functioning. As with much history of technology, this approach is written from the standpoint of successful projects, rather than the standpoint of those designing a technical system, when the outcome is uncertain.

Infrastructure is better seen not as invisible, but as an organisation of processes of testing, reporting, and accounting that attempts to manage the forms of visibility. Every technical apparatus requires maintenance and repair, and is subject to the possibility of malfunction, decay, and failure.

zh: 从失败的可能性可以推出，基础设施不仅是
创造资本的手段，也是摧毁资本的手段。但这并不意味着资本的毁灭仅仅平衡其创造，抵消货币创造的力量。重要的是理解损耗、冗余、破坏、过时和衰败的形式——基础设施使这些形式变得可见，而在把资本主义仅仅视为对“货物”的“消费”的思维方式中，它们不那么明显；同时也要理解伴随任何从未来获取之组织的风险和损失因素。更重要的问题是，攫取装置的技术政治组织如何分配成本、风险和回报。
en: From the possibility of failure, it follows that infrastructures are a

means not only to create capital, but to destroy it. But this does not mean that the destruction of capital simply balances its creation, cancelling out the power of money creation. It is important to understand the forms of wastage, redundancy, sabotage, obsolescence, and decay, all of which are made visible by infrastructures in a way that is less obvious with modes of thinking that focus on capitalism as simply the ‘consumption’ of ‘goods’; and to understand the elements of risk and loss that accompany any organisation of acquisition from the future. The more important issue is how the technopolitical organisation of apparatuses of capture distributes the costs, risks, and rewards.

zh: 基础设施的气候
en: The Climate of Infrastructure

zh: 基础设施作用于时间，但不只以我们通常设想的方式。虽然它们可能加快货物运输、人员旅行或能源流动的速度，这种时间加速也许并非其最重要的属性。其技术耐久性和政治强度赋予它们另一目的。它们引入一种中断，一种未来与当下之间的间隙，当下正是从这个间隙中榨取未来的财富。
en: Infrastructures work on time, but not only in the ways we commonly assume. While they may increase the speed at which goods are transported, people travel, or energy flows, this acceleration of time may not be their most important attribute. Their technical durability and political strength give them another purpose. They introduce an interruption, a gap between the future and the present out of which the present extracts its wealth from the future.

zh: 以这种方式理解资本——把它理解为一种从未来榨取的技术政治过程，基础设施的工作是其例证——为气候危机政治开启了若干问题。这些问题将在最后一章详细讨论。但让我们在此列出这些问题。
en: Understanding capital in this way, as a technopolitical process of extraction from the future, exemplified by the work of infrastructure, opens up several questions for the politics of the climate crisis. These will be taken up in detail in the final chapter. But let us lay out the issues here.

zh: 第一，我们应如何思考增长问题？关于经济增长与气候危机的讨论通常主张，要么必须以不同方式衡量增长，把生态成本计入，要么必须放弃增长目标，代之以去增长政治。如果我们以不同方式理解增长，这些论点会如何变化？与其把增长视为经济扩张的（不充分）衡量，不如把它理解为一种被建构的托词——不仅是为了把某些成本排除在政治考虑之外，而且是为了从范畴上错误再现资本的本质以及我们以未来为代价的生活方式——这样理解会发生什么？
en: First, how should we think about the question of growth? Discussions of economic growth in relation to the climate crisis typically argue either that growth must be measured differently, to take account of ecological costs, or that it must be abandoned as a goal, replaced by a politics of degrowth. How do these arguments change if we consider growth differently? Rather than approaching it as an (inadequate) measure of economic expansion, what happens once we grasp growth as an alibi that has been constructed, not just to exclude certain costs from political consideration, but to categorically misrepresent the nature of capital and our mode of living at the expense of the future?

zh: 第二，我们如何重新构想唯物主义、榨取主义与自然政治的问题？正如
和
所探讨的，我们关于物质生活的许多政治思考仍然陷于生产主义框架，其中
物质的榨取和转化不仅代表一种普遍性的掠夺方式，而且被视为价值创造、人类被治理和剥削之过程的关键。这里提出的替代方案——剩余的实现是绕道和延迟方法的产物，也是组织和控制这些方法的技术政治装置的产物——能否让我们把物质生产看作这些绕道之一，而其中很大部分不是由人类需要、而是由破坏、浪费、故障、衰退和延迟的机会所驱动？
en: Second, how can we reframe questions of materialism, extractivism, and the politics of nature? As
and
explored, much of our political thinking about material life remains caught in the framework of productivism, in which the extraction and transformation of

materials represents not just a pervasive mode of despoliation but the key to the process by which value is created and humans are governed and exploited. Can the alternative suggested here, in which the realisation of surplus is the product of methods of detour and delay, and the technopolitical apparatuses through which these are organised and controlled, allow us to see material production as one among those detours, much of it driven not by human need but by opportunities for sabotage, waste, breakdown, deterioration, and delay.

zh: 第三，衰败、故障和失败的不可避免性，提出了关于基础设施如何作用于时间的进一步问题，这个问题对思考资本和气候危机尤为重要。许多应对气候紧急状态的尝试，都围绕基础设施的再利用或建造巨型新装置展开。正如我们在本书开头所说，基础设施例证了看似独特的人类改造地球的能力。其寿命和规模似乎违抗自然，按照人类目的重造世界。一个多世纪以来，现代基础设施的规模帮助重新定义了人类对自然的体验——驯服河流、照亮城市、穿越地景、征服距离、支配能量的能力。然而，尽管制造了这种人与自然的对立效果，而且实际上帮助变出了自然这一概念本身，基础设施的建设从来不只是人类的成就。
en: Third, the inevitability of decay, breakdown, and failure raises a further question concerning the way in which infrastructures work on time, a question of particular importance for thinking about capital and the climate crisis. Many attempts to address the climate emergency revolve around the repurposing of infrastructures or the building of new apparatuses on a gigantic scale. Infrastructures, as we said at the beginning of this book, exemplify what seems the distinctively human capacity to transform the Earth. Their longevity and size appear to defy nature, remaking the world according to human purposes. For more than a century, the scale of modern infrastructure has helped redefine the human experience of nature – the ability to tame rivers, illuminate cities, cut through landscapes, conquer distances, and command energies. Yet, despite creating this effect of humans versus nature, and, indeed, helping to conjure the very concept of nature, the building of infrastructure was never a human accomplishment alone.

zh: 记住这一点是有益的：我们所设想的人类建构世界的活动，需要大量非人要素，从原材料和建筑设备到能源和计算装置。这些要素不只是被动的投入，而是贡献自身的属性、力量和倾向。它们形成自己的合金与化合物，创造自己的连接和断联层次，贡献稳定持久的倾向，或变得不稳定并引发燃烧。即使是我们所设想的一切复杂、耐久装置中属于人的部分，也由广泛分布的计算、记录、回忆、发送信号和指挥能力构成。每一种这样的能力都是技术、心理和身体成分的混合物，其中人与非人、有意行为与其他倾向之产物之间的确切分界，从来只是一种不确定的效果。
en: It is useful to remember that what we think of as human world-making requires a lot of nonhuman elements, from raw materials and construction equipment to energy sources and calculating devices. These elements are not just passive inputs, but contribute their own properties, powers, and propensities. They form their own alloys and compounds, create their own connections and layers of disconnection, and contribute tendencies to stabilise and endure or become volatile and cause combustion. Even what we think of as the human parts of any complex and enduring apparatus are composed of widely distributed powers to calculate, record, recall, signal, and command. Every such competence is an amalgam of technical, mental, and physical components, in which the exact divide between what is human and nonhuman, between what is intentional and the product of other propensities, is never more than an uncertain effect.

zh: 但基础设施项目的耐久性和规模中，是否仍存在某种独特的人类要素？也许这种观点正是气候危机要我们重新审视的。地球系统比任何看似人类的干预都更
复杂、相互关联和耐久。而我们所再现为大型、巨型项目的，只是享有特别强韧、持久相互关联的局部要素和安排。
en: But does there remain a distinctively human element in the durability and scale of infrastructural projects? Perhaps that is a view that the climate crisis places in perspective. Earth systems turn out to be more

complex, interconnected, and durable than any apparently human intervention. And what we represent as large-scale, mega projects are simply localised elements and arrangements that enjoy particularly strong and durable interconnections.

zh: 最后，我们能否重新思考代际正义问题？这个问题通常被提成气候紧急状态带来的例外问题：当下必须紧急作出什么牺牲，才能让未来有可行的集体生活形式？然而，这里所呈现的理解我们与未来之关系的方法，以不同方式框定了问题。我们的生活方式威胁着后来者，这不仅是我们不顾后果地开发地球资源所造成的副产品，更因为这种生活方式本就建立在从未来夺取生计之上。
en: Finally, can we reconsider the question of intergenerational justice? The question is usually posed as an exceptional issue brought about by the climate emergency. What sacrifices have to be made urgently in the present to allow the possibility of viable forms of collective life in the future? However, the approach presented here to understanding our relation to the future frames the question differently. Our mode of living is a threat to those who come later, not just as a by-product of our own careless exploitation of the resources of the planet, but as a form of life built upon the taking of livelihoods from the future.
